retrieving-memories-cues.alt: Left panel: recall means producing the answer with few cues, as in "Name the part of the brain that forms new memories." Recognition means picking it from options, as in a four-option question listing the cerebellum, hippocampus, amygdala and thalamus. Recognition is usually easier because the options are retrieval cues. Right panel: three ways retrieval improves when the cues at test match learning. Context-dependent memory: the same place, for example words learned underwater are recalled better underwater. State-dependent memory: the same body state, for example learning while calm and recalling better when calm again. Mood-congruent memory: the same mood, for example sad memories come to mind more easily when a person is sad.
